title: Rented media and owned media
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who owns the place where your audience finds you?

Jose said that chapter 9 is short. The three kinds of content are you-driven, which is your personal journey, perspective and intellectual property; news-driven, which uses the news and current events; and relationship-driven.
A student said that the chapter sets up the different kinds of media, rented, owned and earned.
A student said: the algorithms were made to give you success at first, but then they pull the rug out from under you and force you to pay to keep your audience.

Jose gave the example of someone he knew who built a large video-channel business on a platform and lost it when the platform changed. He said you have to make people very aware of you on a platform you own.
Jose said that a local directory owner has her own platform and does not depend on anybody. He said that if you own the content and the channel, you control it.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the platforms where your audience finds you.
Write which you own and which you rent.
Write the one you could own.
Write what you would lose if the rented one changed.
Write the first step to own it.

check.q: What did a student say algorithms do?
choices: Give success at first, then pull the rug
A platform you do not own

check.q: What did Jose say about owning your platform?

recap: Build on a platform you own.
